properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 16 at 10:15PM MST until September 17 at 4:00AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 400 AM MST.

* At 1015 PM MST, An automated river gauge along the Brawley Wash at
Milewide Road indicated a heavy flow of 2300 cfs (cubic feet per
second) that was still rising late this evening. This heavy flow
will still result in flash flooding along and near the Brawley wash
as the water continues to drain into the early morning hours.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Gauges reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Tucson Estates and Picture Rocks.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Manville Rd at Brawley Wash.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 16 at 10:26PM MST until September 17 at 1:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 100 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. It will take
several hours for all the water from these storms to work through
local drainage systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1026 PM MST, Gauge reports indicated several washes still
above alarm stage from the heavy rain earlier due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Apache Wash, New River, Cave Creek, Skunk Creek, Agua Fria River,
North Canyon Creek, Beardsley Canal and Deadman Wash. Additional
rainfall amounts up to 0.75 inches are possible in the warned
area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Phoenix, Glendale, Scottsdale, Peoria, Deer Valley Airport and
Desert Ridge Marketplace.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 17 at 12:59AM MDT until September 17 at 1:30AM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
At 1258 AM MDT, a strong gust front was located along a line
extending from near Hazelton to near Kimberly to Filer, moving east
at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

These severe storms will be near...
Twin Falls, Filer, Hazelton, and Eden around 100 AM MDT.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Wind damage with these storms will occur before any rain or
lightning. Do not wait for the sound of thunder before taking cover.
SEEK SHELTER IMMEDIATELY inside a sturdy structure and stay away from
windows.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 16 at 9:14PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon (US 41) has been steadily
rising since July and on September 15, reached flood stage. The cause
of the high water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is
excessive hydrilla growth (from river bottom to the water surface)
along a 4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.
The hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing
water levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and is forecast to continue.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:45 PM EDT Wednesday was 28.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 28.3 feet.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.4
feet on 08/25/2008.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 200 PM EDT.
